title: Quantum teleportation
kicker: Move an unknown qubit state using one Bell pair and two classical bits.
summary: Alice can transfer an unknown qubit state to Bob without sending the qubit. She uses a shared Bell pair and sends Bob two ordinary bits. Her copy is destroyed in the process, and nothing travels faster than light.

blocks.heading: The setup
blocks.body:
Alice holds a qubit in an unknown state |ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩ (qubit 0). She cannot measure it to learn α and β: a measurement gives one bit and destroys the rest.

Alice and Bob share a Bell pair (|00⟩ + |11⟩)/√2. Alice holds qubit 1 and Bob holds qubit 2.

blocks.heading: The protocol
blocks.body:
1. Alice applies CNOT from qubit 0 to qubit 1, then a Hadamard on qubit 0.

2. She measures qubits 0 and 1, gets two bits m0 and m1, and sends them to Bob over an ordinary channel.

3. Bob applies X to his qubit if m1 = 1, then Z if m0 = 1. His qubit is now exactly |ψ⟩.

blocks.title: Teleporting a state with P(0) = ¾
blocks.caption: Qubit 0 is prepared with RY(π/3), so P(0) = ¾. The measurements and Bob's corrections are written as controlled gates (the deferred-measurement principle gives the same statistics). Bob's qubit ends with P(0) = ¾ and P(1) = ¼.

ops.note: Prepare the state to send: cos(π/6)|0⟩ + sin(π/6)|1⟩ on qubit 0.
Alice: CNOT from her state onto her half of the pair.
Alice: Hadamard on qubit 0. Measuring qubits 0 and 1 now gives Bob's two correction bits.
Bob: Z if m0 = 1. His qubit is now the original state.

blocks.title: Teleporting |1⟩
blocks.caption: With qubit 0 starting in |1⟩, Bob's qubit ends in |1⟩ every time.

blocks.myth: Teleportation sends the qubit instantly, faster than light.
blocks.truth: Until Bob receives Alice's two bits, his qubit is in a 50/50 mixture that carries no information about |ψ⟩. Those bits travel no faster than light, so neither does the state.

blocks.myth: Teleportation makes a copy of the state.
blocks.truth: Alice's measurement leaves her qubits in a basis state, so the original is gone. Only one copy exists at the end, as the no-cloning theorem requires.

blocks.question: Alice measures m0 = 1 and m1 = 0. Which correction does Bob apply?
blocks.hint: X depends on m1 and Z on m0.
blocks.answer: Only Z, because m0 = 1 and m1 = 0.

sources.title: C. H. Bennett et al., "Teleporting an unknown quantum state via dual classical and Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen channels", Physical Review Letters 70, 1895 (1993)
D. Bouwmeester et al., "Experimental quantum teleportation", Nature 390, 575 (1997)
M. A. Nielsen and I. L. Chuang, Quantum Computation and Quantum Information (10th anniversary ed., Cambridge University Press, 2010), ch. 1
